article_notes: Prospective OVAH study: 25 severely anaemic (PCV <= 0.2 L/L) babesiosis dogs (smear diagnosis; South Africa, species not stated, presumably B. rossi) vs 13 healthy reference dogs; samples before any treatment. All Table 1 comparisons (urea, creatinine, cystatin-C, urea:creatinine ratio, free Hb) are infected vs healthy and were not extracted. Extracted only the Discussion case description of 3 haemoconcentrated babesiosis dogs seen during the study period (not part of the 25): one with acute renal failure proven at post mortem (died) vs two that recovered fully; individual values, no test. Creatinine and cystatin-C are close to the definition (renal failure). Units in the text lost the litre symbol ('mmol/ ').

severity_definitions.complication: acute renal failure (fatal, proven at post mortem)
severity_definitions.label: acute renal failure proven on post mortem vs full recovery
severity_definitions.definition: Among three dogs with the haemoconcentrating form of babesiosis seen during the study period, one had acute renal failure proven on post mortem examination and histopathology (died); two made a full recovery.
severity_definitions.quote: The third dog had acute renal failure proven on post mortem examination and histopathology.

associations.quote: The serum urea in this dog was markedly elevated (41.8 mmol/ ) in the presence of markedly elevated serum creatinine (608 µmol/ ) and serum cystatin-C (5.7 mg/ ).
